findings.name: Manaphy
findings.detail: Obtained via a Manaphy Egg Mystery Gift (internet distribution), active November 19, 2021 – February 21, 2022. This was the only way to obtain Manaphy (and, by extension, Phione, which is bred from Manaphy) in BDSP. It was tied to the games' launch window as an early-purchase/loyalty style bonus, not a serial code.
findings.trackable: Once obtained, shows as caught in the National Pokédex (owned/caught flag). No in-game counter tracks 'mythicals obtained' separately.

findings.name: Manaphy — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXPIRED/LIKELY GONE. The distribution window closed February 21, 2022 and every event-tracking source consulted (Serebii's dedicated distribution tracker, which lists every past and current BDSP event) marks it 'Expired' with no listed re-run, permanent code, or QR-code alternative. No news of any re-distribution was found in a search covering years after the window closed. Absence of evidence is not proof it can never return, but there is no indication Nintendo has ever re-run a BDSP Mystery Gift distribution.
sources: Bing search summary — no re-distribution news found (fetched)

findings.name: Shaymin
findings.detail: Obtained via the 'Oak's Letter' Mystery Gift item, active February 27 – March 27, 2022 (timed to Pokémon Day). The letter unlocks access to the Flower Paradise, reached via a white stone on Route 224, where Shaymin (Lv. 30) is encountered.
findings.trackable: Shows as caught in the National Pokédex once obtained.

findings.name: Shaymin — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXPIRED/LIKELY GONE. Window closed March 27, 2022. Serebii's distribution tracker marks it 'Expired' with no re-run listed anywhere. No evidence found of any subsequent re-distribution as of today.

findings.name: Darkrai
findings.detail: Obtained via the 'Member Card' Mystery Gift item, active April 1–30, 2022. The card grants access to New Moon Island, reached from the Canalave City inn (available after beating the Elite Four), where Darkrai (Lv. 50) is encountered.
findings.trackable: Shows as caught in the National Pokédex once obtained.

findings.name: Darkrai — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXPIRED/LIKELY GONE. Window closed April 30, 2022. Serebii's distribution tracker marks it 'Expired' with no re-run listed. No evidence found of any subsequent re-distribution.

findings.name: Mew — conflict resolved
findings.detail: RESOLVED: Both reported methods were actually describing the same mechanic, not competing alternatives. Mew is obtained in an in-game location (Floaroma Town) FROM an NPC (an old woman) WHO ONLY appears/gives the Pokémon if the game detects save data from Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! or Let's Go, Eevee! on the same Nintendo Switch console (i.e., that game has been played/saved on the system, associated with a user profile). It is not a pure walk-up encounter, and it is not solely an external save-check with no in-game location — it is both at once. Mew is given at Level 1.
findings.trackable: Shows as caught in the National Pokédex once obtained.
sources: Bulbapedia: List of in-game event Pokémon in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl (fetched, quoted: 'An old woman gives the player a Mew if they have save data from Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! or Let's Go, Eevee!')
Bulbapedia: Mythical Pokémon article (fetched, corroborates Let's Go save-data requirement)

findings.name: Mew — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXTERNALLY GATED BUT OBTAINABLE. This is a save-data-detection mechanic, not a Mystery Gift or time-limited distribution — it has no announced expiration date. A player starting fresh today needs to own and have played (with save data present) Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! or Let's Go, Eevee! on the same Switch console/profile as their BDSP save. Both Let's Go titles remain purchasable/downloadable on the Switch eShop as of this research, so this path remains open to any player willing to acquire and boot that second game. No source found indicates this detection has ever been disabled or is time-limited.
sources: Bulbapedia: List of in-game event Pokémon in BDSP (fetched)

findings.name: Jirachi
findings.detail: Obtained in Floaroma Town from an NPC (an old man) who gives Jirachi (Level 5) only if the game detects save data from Pokémon Sword or Pokémon Shield on the same Nintendo Switch console. Same mechanic family as the Mew method (both NPCs are in Floaroma Town, gated on different linked games).
findings.trackable: Shows as caught in the National Pokédex once obtained.
sources: Bulbapedia: List of in-game event Pokémon in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl (fetched, quoted: 'An old man gives the player a Jirachi if they have save data from Pokémon Sword or Shield')

findings.name: Jirachi — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXTERNALLY GATED BUT OBTAINABLE. Confirmed accurate: requires Sword/Shield save data on the same console, no time limit involved (it's a save-detection check, not an online distribution). Sword and Shield remain purchasable on the Switch eShop, so this route remains open to any player who acquires and saves progress in either title.
sources: Bulbapedia: List of in-game event Pokémon in BDSP (fetched)

findings.name: Arceus
findings.detail: Added via the version 1.3.0 game update, but the update alone does NOT grant Arceus. The mechanic requires: (1) BDSP updated to v1.3.0 or later, AND (2) Pokémon Legends: Arceus save data detected on the same console with ALL missions in that game's story completed (one source specified this as all 27 missions, unverified against a second source). When conditions are met, an Azure Flute is delivered to the player's house in Twinleaf Town. The player must also have already caught Dialga or Palkia, entered the Hall of Fame, and obtained the National Pokédex in BDSP. Using the Azure Flute at Spear Pillar reshapes the map into a staircase leading to the Hall of Origin, where Arceus (Level 80) can be encountered.
findings.trackable: Shows as caught in the National Pokédex once obtained.
sources: Bulbapedia: Mythical Pokémon article (fetched, corroborates Legends: Arceus save-data + v1.3.0 requirement)

findings.name: Arceus — current obtainability verdict
findings.detail: VERDICT: EXTERNALLY GATED BUT OBTAINABLE, NOT purely a patch-based unlock. Every current copy of BDSP will already be on v1.3.0+ (it's an old, presumably mandatory-by-now patch), so that part is a non-issue for a fresh start today. However, the gating factor a designer must not overlook is the Pokémon Legends: Arceus save-data requirement with full story completion — this is an external game requirement, not just 'have the patch.' No time limit is attached to this mechanic (it is not an online Mystery Gift); Legends: Arceus remains purchasable on the Switch eShop. This path should remain open indefinitely to a player willing to also complete Legends: Arceus.

gaps: Could not run new WebSearch queries after the session's search budget (200/200) was exhausted partway through this task; all findings after that point rely on WebFetch against specific known URLs (Serebii, Bulbapedia, one Bing results page), not fresh targeted searches. Treat the 'EXPIRED/LIKELY GONE' verdicts as very probable but not airtight.

Only wiki-level detail was available.
